title: Tuning Spark — memory management and parallelism (Apache Spark documentation)

claims.text: Spark's unified memory manager holds execution memory (shuffles, joins, sorts, aggregations) and storage memory (cached and broadcast blocks) in one shared region rather than as fixed partitions, so when execution is idle storage may take the whole region and vice versa.

spark.memory.fraction defaults to 0.6 and sizes the shared execution/storage region as a fraction of the JVM heap minus a fixed 300 MiB reservation; the remaining 40% is deliberately left for user data structures, Spark's internal metadata, and headroom against out-of-memory errors from unusually large records.

spark.memory.storageFraction defaults to 0.5 and does not partition memory — it sets the floor of storage memory that execution is not permitted to evict; above that floor, execution can reclaim space from storage by evicting cached blocks, while storage can never evict execution.

The asymmetry that execution can evict storage but storage cannot evict execution is why raising spark.memory.storageFraction to protect a cache commonly causes the spill it was meant to prevent: the guaranteed cache floor is taken out of the memory execution would otherwise borrow.
Apache Spark's parallelism guidance is 2–3 tasks per CPU core in the cluster, so that a straggler task does not leave most cores idle waiting for the final wave of work.
